takes.jeremiyah love: Widely viewed as the top dynasty RB in this class, praised for explosive vision and pass-catching, seen as a likely early first-round SF rookie pick.
takes.fernando mendoza: Consensus QB1 buzz has grown after a strong, efficient Indiana season, with analysts framing him as a rare early-round SF quarterback investment.
takes.carnell tate: Ranked among the top-two rookie wideouts by most dynasty analysts, valued for elite route-running and target volume in a pro-style Ohio State offense.
takes.jordyn tyson: Rising WR2/WR3 in early rookie boards after big-play production at Arizona State, though a lingering injury history keeps some rankers slightly cautious.
takes.makai lemon: Trending up dynasty analysts' lists as a versatile slot/outside threat, with strong target-share metrics from USC boosting his early Day 2 profile.
takes.jadarian price: Viewed as a change-of-pace complement more than a lead back, with rankers noting his explosiveness but capped ceiling behind Notre Dame's committee usage.
takes.kc concepcion: Gaining momentum as a shifty slot receiver comp, with analysts citing his after-catch ability from Texas A&M as reason for a rising rookie ADP.
takes.ty simpson: Seen as a solid QB2 in dynasty rookie classes, praised for accuracy and decision-making at Alabama but lacking elite arm talent some SF drafters want.
takes.kenyon sadiq: Emerging TE1 in this class per most analysts, valued for athletic upside and receiving role at Oregon that projects well to early-down usage.
takes.omar cooper: Generally slotted as a mid-tier WR3/WR4 rookie, with rankers citing solid hands and route polish but a less explosive overall profile.
takes.denzel boston: Steadily climbing boards as a big-bodied contested-catch winner at Washington, with analysts liking his red-zone role and size-speed combination.
takes.eli stowers: Regarded as a top-three rookie TE due to receiving-first tight end/hybrid usage at Vanderbilt that translates well to modern fantasy scoring.
takes.nicholas singleton: Ranked as a solid RB2 rookie option, with analysts noting his explosive big-play speed but some concern over shared Penn State backfield touches.
takes.jonah coleman: Viewed as an underrated bruising early-down back, with rankers pointing to strong contact balance and receiving improvement at Washington.
takes.antonio williams: Typically ranked as a depth WR4/WR5 rookie, praised for reliable hands but considered a complementary piece rather than a true alpha at Clemson.
takes.germie bernard: Seen as a solid but unspectacular depth receiver prospect, with analysts citing steady production but a lack of standout separation traits at Alabama.
takes.emmett johnson: Gaining late-riser buzz as an efficient, versatile back, with rankers highlighting his receiving chops out of Nebraska's backfield.
takes.zachariah branch: Ranked as a boom/bust slot-speed receiver, with analysts noting elite return/YAC ability but inconsistent target share concerns at Georgia.
takes.chris bell: Generally viewed as a late-round dynasty flier, with scouts citing big-play speed at Louisville but concerns about overall route consistency.
takes.dezhaun stribling: Considered a solid depth WR prospect, with rankers noting reliable veteran-college production at Ole Miss but a capped athletic ceiling.
takes.elijah sarratt: Praised as an underrated size-speed possession receiver, with analysts citing strong contested-catch numbers at Indiana as reason for rising stock.
takes.carson beck: Ranked as a back-end rookie QB, with analysts split on his ceiling given inconsistent tape and turnover concerns during his final college season.
takes.mike washington: Viewed as a deep-league dynasty stash, with rankers citing raw explosiveness at Arkansas but a lack of clear early-down role clarity.
takes.kaytron allen: Seen as a committee-limited RB4/RB5 rookie option, with analysts noting solid power but reduced standalone value in Penn State's rotation.
takes.malachi fields: Generally ranked as a sleeper big-slot receiver, with scouts citing physical tools at Notre Dame but limited target volume as a concern.
takes.chris brazzell: Viewed as a boom/bust vertical threat, with analysts praising big-play speed at Tennessee but citing inconsistent hands as a red flag.
takes.cade klubnik: Ranked toward the back of rookie QB boards, with rankers citing solid accuracy at Clemson but below-average ceiling for superflex purposes.
takes.oscar delp: Considered a late-round TE stash, with analysts noting blocking-first usage at Georgia limiting his receiving upside relative to top TE prospects.
